source.section: PDF p10 Line 4 'What pensions are exempt?' first bullet (contributory pension of the Commonwealth: enter 0 in line 4); Form 1 lines 2a, 2c, 9 (Schedule X line 2, PDF p20), 10-22

worked: Federal AGI = Massachusetts state employee contributory pension 45,000.00 (person 0) + IRA distribution 30,000.00 (person 0) = 75,000.00 (given). Federal taxable income = 75,000.00 - 17,750.00 standard deduction (15,750.00 + 1 x 2,000.00 age 65 or older) = 57,250.00 (given, not tested; the federal senior deduction is ignored). Massachusetts Form 1 (the projection starts from federal AGI and takes out the exempt items): Line 4 taxable pensions = 0.00 for the 45,000.00 Massachusetts state employee contributory pension (exempt: contributory pension of the Commonwealth, PDF p10 first bullet; enter 0 in line 4) = 0.00. Line 9 (Schedule X line 2 worksheet: 30,000.00 IRA distributions less 0.00 contributions previously taxed by Massachusetts) = 30,000.00. Line 10 total 5.0% income = 30,000.00. Line 16 total deductions = 0.00. Line 17 = 30,000.00 - 0.00 = 30,000.00. Line 2a personal exemption (single) = 4,400.00; line 2c age 65 or over before 2026: 1 x 700.00 = 700.00; line 2g = line 18 = 5,100.00. Line 19 = 30,000.00 - 5,100.00 = 24,900.00. Line 20 interest and dividends = 0.00. Line 21 = 24,900.00. Line 22 = 24,900.00 x 0.05 = 1,245.00. No 8.5%/12% income or long-term gains (lines 23-24 = 0.00); 4% surtax 0.00 (line 21 is under 1,083,150). Line 28 total tax = 1,245.00; no credits (No Tax Status and the Limited Income Credit do not apply: Massachusetts AGI 30,000.00 is over their limits). State income tax = 1,245.00.
